pr_body:
I have implemented a plugin architecture (`MultiModelPlugin`) over `MultiModalData` to define how each modality type should be preprocessed before being passed to the model as keyword arguments. This preserves the contract between the output of HuggingFace processor and the input into the HuggingFace model. As long as those keyword arguments do not conflict with the ones we have in vLLM, I think this is a good way to make the framework flexible enough to support other multi-modal architectures.

FIX #4054 (the data is now automatically converted into the model's device)

### Related Contributions

This PR is part of #3978.

This PR also implements Proposals 1 and 3 of #4194.

### Features
1. Refactor of `MultiModalData`
    - Image input is now split into two subclasses:
        - `ImageFeatureData` represents the image features of LLaVA after being passed through the vision tower, but before the multi-modal projection is applied.
        - `ImagePixelData` represents the raw image (using `PIL.Image` class). `AutoImageProcessor` from HuggingFace is loaded from `config.json` to pre-process input images before being passed to the model as `pixel_values`. As with the tokenizer, you can override the default one and specify the version of image processor via `EngineConfig`; you can even disable image preprocessing altogether, which is useful if you want to pass in images that have already been preprocessed.
    - The LLaVA implementation has been updated accordingly to accept the new inputs.
2. A new documentation page for using VLMs can be found under ([dev/multimodal](https://github.com/DarkLight1337/vllm-rocm/blob/mm-data-processor/docs/source/dev/multimodal.rst)).

### Compatibility Changes

- `pillow` will be upgraded to a `common` dependency (from `dev`) to process the images.

issue_context.title: [Bug]: Incorrect Data Type Conversion for MultiModalData
issue_context.body:
### Your current environment

```text
The output of `python collect_env.py`
```


### 🐛 Describe the bug

I've encountered an issue with the code in the vllm project on GitHub. Specifically, at line 170 of the llm.py file https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/entrypoints/llm.py#L170, there is a conversion of multi_modal_data.data to torch.float16 using the statement multi_modal_data.data = multi_modal_data.data.to(torch.float16). This automatic conversion may not be suitable for all use cases, especially if the model is designed to operate with bfloat16 or other numerical precisions. If this is an issue that needs to be addressed, I would be happy to submit a pull request with a fix
comments: I have refactored the processing logic in #3978 which removes the assumption of `float16` data type. Could you suggest a test case to determine whether the conversion problem still exists or not?

review_comments: Why do we need to define these two? Are these defined for line length purposes?
They provide the generic type parameters used in `MultiModalPlugin` and `MultiModalRegistry`.
Just a nit: I don't think we need to create the `mm_data` variable here?

Yeah - what I meant really was that we can simply do

`mm_kwargs = self.multi_modal_input_processor(seq_group_metadata.multi_modal_data)`

since `mm_data` is not used anywhere else in this function:

The variable is also used in the `if` statement. I made an intermediate variable to avoid exceeding the line length limit in `mm_kwargs = self.multi_modal_input_processor(seq_group_metadata.multi_modal_data)`.

Could you add a docstring here to explain the purpose of this class and the plugins? (I personally understand it, but I think it's a bit vague to developers who are new to the multimodal work and this file)
I have added a new section to the vLLM documentation to explain this.
